summary: The study examines the nucleation and growth during tungsten (W) atomic layer deposition (ALD) on aluminum oxide (Al2O3) surfaces and Al2O3 ALD on W surfaces. W ALD was performed using alternating exposures of WF6 and Si2H6, while Al2O3 ALD used Al(CH3)3 and H2O. AES measurements revealed that 3 WF6/Si2H6 reaction cycles were needed to nucleate W ALD on Al2O3 at 473 K, with a growth rate of 2.6–3.5 Å per cycle. For Al2O3 ALD on W at 450 K, one H2O/Al(CH3)3 cycle was sufficient for nucleation, with a growth rate of 1.0 Å per cycle. The study highlights the importance of nucleation and growth mechanisms for the fabrication of W/Al2O3 nanolaminates with potential applications in X-ray mirrors, thermal barrier coatings, and tribological films.
